t: Liquidity measures on the Polish sovereign panel
s: Cross-sectional medians of standard microstructure liquidity measures across the BondSpot panel, monthly from 2005 to today. Data are computed at the bond-day level and aggregated to monthly cross-sectional medians (means for ZTD and the composite z-score). Read the short — "Six microstructure measures, one composite" Seminar slides — 14 slides, full screen Sample period — mont
Cross-sectional median (line) plus 25th–75th percentile band across the BondSpot panel each month. Spreads in basis points of yield, computed from BondSpot best bid and best ask fixings.
Average share of bond-days within the cross-section for which no trades occurred. A higher series indicates a less continuously-traded panel.

Standardised average of the underlying liquidity measures (BAS, Amihud, Roll, gamma, Corwin-Schultz, ZTD), with positive values indicating less liquid markets and negative values indicating more liquid markets relative to the panel-period mean.
Cross-sectional median of the Amihud (2002) ratio: |daily return| / daily turnover. Higher values indicate larger price impact per unit traded.
Cross-sectional median of the Roll (1984) implicit spread estimator: 2 × √(-cov(Δp_t, Δp_{t-1})). Set to NA where the autocovariance is positive.
Cross-sectional median of the Corwin-Schultz (2012) high-low spread estimator. A robust intra-day spread proxy that doesn't require quote data.

t: The Polish duration trade pays over cash, except in the 2022 storm
s: TBSP compounded at 4.14% per year since end-2006. Carry and roll-down contributed +413 bp per year on average; the macro-driven curve-move bloc averaged -17 bp per year and is statistically indistinguishable from zero. t: No simple recipe beats the bond benchmark
p: No simple recipe beats the bond benchmark
s: Two-page short on term-premium duration timing against the TBSP benchmark. A full-sample term premium manufactures a carry strategy that reverses sign the moment it is estimated in real time. Once estimation is honest, no rule reliably beats the benchmark after the search, the costs and out-of-sample markets.
